q: An IT administrator wants to simplify user provisioning by assigning shared folder permissions to specific job titles rather than configuring individual user accounts. Which access control scheme should be implemented?
opts: Mandatory access control governed by classification tags
Discretionary access control managed by resource owners
Role-based access control mapped to defined job duties
Rule-based access control dictated by system parameters
exp: Role-based access control (RBAC) binds permissions to functional roles rather than individuals, streamlining provisioning when users join or change positions.

wrongFeedback.0: Mandatory access control (MAC) restricts access based on fixed data classification labels and user clearance levels, not organizational job titles.
wrongFeedback.1: Discretionary access control (DAC) allows individual resource owners to decide who can access files, which increases administrative overhead.
wrongFeedback.3: Rule-based access control applies operational constraints (such as time-of-day restrictions or firewall rules) rather than user job functions.

q: A clinic permits physicians to view patient records, but wants to block access if a physician attempts to log in from a personal smartphone outside the hospital network. Why is standard role-based access control alone insufficient to enforce this policy?
opts: It grants access based on user job functions rather than dynamic environmental factors
It delegates authorization decisions to individual data owners rather than central policy
It enforces mandatory security clearance tags that override temporary connection rules
It permits higher-tier medical accounts to automatically inherit lower-tier permissions
exp: Standard RBAC makes static authorization decisions based strictly on assigned roles; it lacks native mechanisms to evaluate runtime contextual attributes like device ownership, network location, or IP address (which requires ABAC).

wrongFeedback.1: Delegating authorization to individual data owners describes discretionary access control (DAC), not an architectural limitation of RBAC.
wrongFeedback.2: Security clearance tags and mandatory labels characterize mandatory access control (MAC), which is not part of standard RBAC deployments.
wrongFeedback.3: Role inheritance allows senior tiers to inherit subordinate privileges, but it does not cause or explain the inability to inspect incoming network connections.
